title: AT&T (T) Q3 Earnings and Revenues Top Estimates
author: Na
description: AT&T reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.65 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.61, with revenues of $32.32 billion exceeding expectations by 2.02%. Despite the earnings beat, AT&T shares have declined 5.7% year-to-date compared to the S&P 500's 12.7% gain. The stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While AT&T beat earnings and revenue estimates with a +6.56% EPS surprise, the stock has significantly underperformed the broader market year-to-date (-5.7% vs S&P 500 +12.7%). The Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating indicates expected market-level performance going forward, suggesting mixed investor sentiment despite positive earnings results.

title: SpaceX Is Buying Airwaves to Take On the Wireless Carriers. Is the Stock a Buy?
author: Daniel Sparks
description: SpaceX agreed to purchase Grain Management's 800 MHz spectrum portfolio for approximately $8 billion to enhance Starlink Mobile's indoor coverage capabilities. While the deal threatens traditional wireless carriers, the analyst argues SpaceX stock remains overvalued at over 80 times sales, with meaningful revenue from mobile service still over a year away.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite strategic spectrum acquisition strengthening Starlink Mobile, the stock is valued at over 80 times sales with significant losses in the first half of 2026. The $8 billion deal represents less than 1% of the company's $2 trillion market cap, and meaningful revenue from mobile service is over a year away, making the stock appear overpriced.

title: SpaceX Is Changing: Here's What You Need to Know
author: Rich Smith
description: SpaceX is transitioning from a pure space launch company to an AI and telecommunications giant. While the company will reduce launch frequency in 2026-2027 as it retires Falcon 9 rockets, larger Starship vehicles will compensate with greater payload capacity. The real growth opportunity lies in Starlink's expansion into mobile telecommunications, with V3 satellites promising 100x bandwidth increase. SpaceX recently acquired $8 billion in cellular spectrum licenses to become a major U.S. mobile carrier, rivaling Verizon and AT&T.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: SpaceX is executing strategic growth initiatives with record launch numbers in 2025, successful Starlink V3 deployment, and aggressive expansion into telecommunications with $8 billion spectrum acquisition. Starlink's profitability ($5.3B operating profit) and potential to reach $140B revenue provides strong near-term growth catalyst.

SpaceX's explicit goal to become a major U.S. mobile carrier rivaling Verizon represents direct competitive threat to its core telecommunications business, potentially disrupting traditional carrier market share.
